rationale: The assistant got the model and sensibly ruled out the hose, and once the customer volunteered the burning smell and sparks it issued a clear stop-use and professional referral, which is the right boundary. However it never asked about smells, heat or sparking despite a 12-year-old Henry with a rough growl and lost speed, showed weak product knowledge ('near the battery compartment', 'brush bar' on a plain-head cylinder) and kept steering to the floorhead after the customer said suction was weak at the hose end. The final hypothesis of 'motor bearings' or 'internal wiring' misses the far more likely worn carbon brushes/commutator, and no cost-versus-replacement or Numatic service context was offered.
